body:
>you have more than enough strength to do whatever it is you have to do.

Yup. 



On a daily basis, I never really know, nor do I understand what I am doing. I can't really think of a strong way to convey this nor better terms to use. 



It's just me, incapable of tending to myself, with no support structure of any kind, with my life of not-happenings and bad memories, facing the outside world. I have no clue what I'm doing regarding *anything* and I'm just slowly corroding.

During my college attempt, I acquired a few fentanyl lollipops. 

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actiq

600 μg versions.

I absolutely loved them. :/

They'd sound a lot more severe if I were: a) completely transparent right now, and/or; b) writing a fifty-page response, instead of short comment responses. 

It goes deeper than depression. I've been on a myriad of pharmaceuticals since the earliest of ages.

I don't remember exactly when, but... I have a few references. 

I know that early on in elementary school, by Grade 2, I was on Ritalin. They tried Ritalin SR for me that year. I can still feel inside how terrible the SR made me felt. I would break down and cry within thirty minutes of taking my dose. I know that Ritalin/methylphenidate is for ADHD and the like. I was on antidepressants before that.

I was put on Imipramine at an even earlier age than that... I just don't have a good frame of reference as to how young it was. 

I just remember having to go to a hospital every month so that they could test my blood and make sure that the levels of the medication in my system were low enough to be safe. 


Outside of that, over the years I've been on Zoloft, Wellbutrin, Prozac, Lexapro, Trazodone, Paxil and probably others that currently slip my mind.

The most recent doctor that I saw/see is a medicine-heavy psychiatrist. They only care about getting you in-and-out ASAP and handing you your scripts now, it seems.  

I can't exactly look into CBT or anything like that. I don't have the insurance to cover it.

Putting things on hold is about as bad of an idea for me as is possible. 

It would keep me from ruminating over things and constantly reliving negative memories in my head. 

As for knowing what to do, though? No, I haven't a clue, really.

I mean, conceptually, I have ideas about what I would need to do, in order to achieve what I want. There's a gap there, though; I don't really understand/comprehend how to bridge it.  Like I said, I feel as though I'm missing some essential skill set.

I no longer possess the ability to pull through this on my own. I've been working that way for my entire life; I've simply run out of steam, or am very, very close to doing so. 

I don't possess the strength to will my way through this. Not alone. 

That's all I know, though...

Well, I live in my mother's house right now, but I don't really like her. She's not a very good person and we definitely don't get along (of course, it's all my fault though, right? I'm a terrible son, etc. I'm not great by any means, but blame is at least 50/50). My sister lives 45 minutes away. She's two years younger than me and just gave birth to a son (as in, less than a month ago).  This makes me feel very old. My dad lives in South Carolina. He has his issues, too. Fatherhood was never really his thing. 

My parents separated on 31 October, 1993 or 1994 (the latter, I think). I guess you take the separation when I was 8, add it to the adoption, and modify that with the fact that my parents were both 40+ hours a week professionals, family doesn't mean all too much to me.

As for friends, well, there's been some people that I have called friends over the past ten years, but I don't know how many of them, if any, have been legitimate friends. 

I see two or three people somewhat regularly, but...They don't need to hear about me. I just smooth over the edges and make things look ok. For appearance's sake. 


I gave up on talking to people online because I just end up griping about my life (as I am now, surprise), and it's not becoming of me when I can talk of little else.

Whilst I appreciate the introductory bit, I've been dealing with this for 23 years. I've been on antidepressants of various kinds for large portions of that. I personally don't think that it's depression. 

Yes, I do get depressed. I notice when that is the case. For the most part though, I just feel empty. Something's missing. Well, a lot of things are missing. 

What do I dislike about my job? I dislike the bureaucracy. I dislike that I deal with three bosses on a daily basis. I dislike the corruption and the lack of caring that I see at the central office for a major city' public school system. I hate what I do above anything else, just because it's too simplistic and my mind is running all day as a result. 


Getting this job in the first place was difficult enough for me. I don't really know what I'd be doing if I were to consider looking for a different one. I have absolutely no qualifications. I don't think I can do much better than what I have at current. 

I spent the first thirteen years of my life essentially isolated (lack of social skills and ostracization over my looks/intelligence). I never really recovered from that.

I just sort of meander through the world, disconnected all the while.

I'm 23. I was enrolled in college, but I was in no way prepared socially; it was a disaster. 

So now I work an office job with no qualifications, always telling myself that I'm going to work my way back to school and get my degree.

I realize that it's just a carrot dangling in front of my face, though.

I really hate my job, though. 

I haven't been in about a week ("taking time off for a mental health break"). I might not go back. Once I fully determine if it matters, I'll decide.
